text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Majority of pensions experts in ruling Christian Democrats (CDU) backs Labour Minister Norbert Bluem's reform plans.
- Police end Greenpeace blockade of Kruemmel nuclear power station.
- DAX share index hits record high.
- Workers in printing industry strike in support of pay claim.
HANDELSBLATT
- Bluem moves closer to his critics on issue of taxing pensions.
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl set to lauch construction of new chancellery in Berlin.
- Construction giant Hochtief looks interested in taking over rival Holzmann.
- Germans saving more and more for house construction.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Reform of property-owning laws sparks boom in savings for house construction.
- Technology Minister Juergen Ruettgers wants to coordinate chemistry courses at universities more closely with industry.
- Concentration of ownership in retail sector continues to increase.
DIE WELT
- Officials from federal and regional government endorse slaughter of 5,200 British and Swiss cattle in move to calm fears about mad cow disease.
- Opposition Social Democrats want leaner, more efficient state.
- 404,000 fewer jobs in Germany in 1996 compared to the previous year, official statistics show.
- Germany still lags behind other countries in private property ownership.
